nodes.summary: There is a real constant $C$ such that for every natural number $n$, the number of line-compatible sequences for $n$, that is, of distinct multisets of the numbers $|\ell \cap P|$ over the distinct lines $\ell$ through two distinct points of an $n$-point set $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$, each line counted once, is at most $e^{C \sqrt{n}}$. This answers Erdős Problem 733.
nodes.title: Szemerédi–Trotter bound on line-compatible sequences

nodes.summary: The proposition that there is a real constant $C$ such that for every natural number $n$, the number $f(n)$ of line-compatible sequences for $n$ is at most $e^{C \sqrt{n}}$; that is, there are at most $\exp(O(\sqrt{n}))$ line-compatible sequences. This is Erdős Problem 733.
nodes.title: Subexponential count of line-compatible sequences (statement)

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, $f(n)$ is the number of distinct multisets that arise as the line sizes of some $n$-point set $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$, that is, as the multiset of the numbers $|\ell \cap P|$ over the distinct lines $\ell$ through two distinct points of $P$, each line counted once. These multisets are the line-compatible sequences for $n$; there are finitely many, since each has at most $n^2$ entries,…
nodes.title: Number of line-compatible sequences

nodes.summary: For a finite set $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$, let $A(P)$ be the set of the numbers $|\ell \cap P|$ over the lines $\ell$ through at least two distinct points of $P$, and let $F(n)$ be the number of distinct sets $A(P)$ over all $n$-point sets $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$. There is a real constant $C$ such that $F(n) \le e^{C\sqrt{n}}$ for every natural number $n$.
nodes.title: Szemerédi–Trotter bound for line-incidence sets (Erdős Problem 607)

nodes.summary: For a finite set $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$, let $A(P)$ be the set of the numbers $|\ell \cap P|$ over the lines $\ell$ through at least two distinct points of $P$, and let $F(n)$ be the number of distinct sets $A(P)$ over all $n$-point sets $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$. This is the statement that there is a real constant $C$ such that $F(n) \le e^{C\sqrt{n}}$ for every natural number $n$, that is,…
nodes.title: Erdős Problem 607: subexponentially many line-incidence sets

nodes.summary: For a finite set $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$, let $A(P)$ be the set of the numbers $|\ell \cap P|$ over the lines $\ell$ through at least two distinct points of $P$. For a natural number $n$, $F(n)$ is the number of distinct sets $A(P)$ over all $n$-point sets $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$. Every such $A(P)$ is a subset of $\{0, \dots, n\}$.
nodes.title: Number of line-incidence sets

nodes.summary: For a finite set $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$, $A(P)$ is the set of the numbers $|\ell \cap P|$ over the lines $\ell$ determined by $P$, that is, the lines through at least two distinct points of $P$.
nodes.title: Line-incidence set of a finite planar point set

nodes.summary: For a finite set $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$, this is the multiset of the numbers $|\ell \cap P|$, where $\ell$ ranges over the lines determined by $P$, that is, the distinct lines through two distinct points of $P$, each counted once.
nodes.title: Line sizes of a planar point set
